title: Physical-mental interplay of mental and somatic health across the lifespan: Fatigue in different physical-mental conditions
summary: Fatigue refers to subjectively perceived or objectively measurable tiredness, exhaustion and listlessness and is reported by 5-20% of the general population. Fatigue occurs in numerous medical contexts and is one of the most common symptoms reported by patients in primary care. Fatigue is common in psychiatric and psychosomatic disorders as well as in somatic diseases such as cancer, multiple sclerosis, type 1 diabetes mellitus, chronic kidney and liver disease, chronic inflammatory bowel disease, post-COVID syndrome and chronic fatigue syndrome. The aim of this project is to investigate fatigue in different patient cohorts with relevant physical and psychological factors (physical-mental interplay) and to comprehensively characterise different dimensions of the symptoms. The results will form the basis for the development of tailored therapeutic approaches in future projects.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
The inclusion criteria depend on the respective patient cohorts: 

Somatoform disorders: Diagnosed somatoform disorder F45.xx

Multiple sclerosis: Confirmed MS diagnosis according to the valid McDonald criteria (from 2017)

Type 1 diabetes mellitus: Confirmed diagnosis of type 1 diabetes mellitus

Malignant tumours: Confirmed diagnosis of a malignant tumour

Chronic renal failure: Current dialysis treatment

Chronic liver disease: Primary biliary cholangitis or
cirrhosis of the liver Child A-C

Chronic inflammatory bowel disease: Ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease

Post-COVID: Diagnosis of post-COVID syndrome (at least 1 symptom ≥12 weeks after infection)

Chronic fatigue syndrome: Diagnosis according to Canadian criteria (International Consensus Criteria 2003)
Exclusion criteria:
The following exclusion criteria apply to all patient cohorts: 

- Insufficient knowledge of the German language
- Pregnancy
- Breastfeeding

For the multiple sclerosis, type 1 diabetes mellitus, chronic renal failure, chronic liver disease, chronic inflammatory bowel disease, post-COVID and chronic fatigue syndrome cohorts, the following exclusion criterion also applies:

- Malignant tumours in the medical history

For the multiple sclerosis cohort, the following exclusion criterion also applies: 

- Indication of a current relapse (within the last 30 days)
